- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 5% of prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce volatility bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; favor sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days over pure trend.
